title: Probabilistic kernel selector and staged prefill strategy to mitigate FlashAttn v3 tail regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: We observed intermittent p99 prefill tail regressions after enabling FlashAttention v3 for several model families. Root cause investigation suggests v3 produces higher memory fragmentation and occasional kernel mis-selection for short-start long-decode workloads, which increases prefill latency under specific batch/seq-length shapes. This ticket implements a probabilistic runtime kernel selector paired with a staged prefill warmup (micro-batching the first N tokens) to reduce tail latency while keeping v3 benefits for median throughput. Goals: 1) reduce p99 prefill latency by >=20% on affected shapes, 2) avoid regressing median throughput by more than 5%, 3) surface deterministic telemetry for later autotuner decisions.
acceptance_criteria: New selector can choose between flashattn v2, flashattn v3, and a conservative v2-compatible fallback at runtime
End-to-end p99 prefill latency improvement >=20% on benchmark shapes listed in design doc
No more than 5% regression in median tokens/sec on standard throughput suites
Selector emits telemetry fields: chosen_kernel, confidence_score, fallback_reason, warmup_microbatch_size
Implementation covered by unit tests and a performance CI job; PR merged to main
Rollout flag gated; ability to rollback to previous kernel policy without restart
implementation_notes: Add lightweight confidence estimator: heuristics based on batch_size, seq_len_distribution, public KV cache hit expectation — implemented as <10µs decision path
Probabilistic selector uses a soft-explore policy in early rollout: P(v3)=conf, else choose v2/fallback. Conf is scaled from estimator output with clamp(0.1, 0.95)
Staged prefill: micro-batch first 8 tokens (configurable) to establish cache warmness and avoid cold-start kernel mispredictions
Autotuner integration: log outcomes to /metrics/runtime/kernel_selector.v1 with tags for model, region, deployment_type
Add mutex/serialization to avoid rapid kernel thrash when multiple concurrent requests with divergent shapes arrive
Add a feature flag runtime.kernelselector.strategy=probabilistic_staged for safe rollout
decisions: Do not change existing kernel implementations in this ticket — only selection policy and scheduling logic
Prefer a conservative confidence floor (0.1) to ensure continued exploration and telemetry collection
Warmup microbatch size initial value = 8 tokens; will tune based on perf CI results
Telemetry schema chosen to be minimal to avoid high cardinality: chosen_kernel, conf_bucket, seq_len_bucket, batch_size_bucket
tradeoffs: Pros: measurable p99 reduction on affected shapes; continued ability to leverage v3 for median and high-throughput cases
Cons: scheduler complexity increases; small added latency for decision path (~5-10µs) and possible slight throughput loss during warmup microbatches
Operational: requires new dashboards and alerting to detect misclassification or thrashing
